# OpenCode Plugin Lab A disposable, isolated Docker test lab for **OpenCode V2 plugins**. Point it at any plugin and it builds the plugin, loads it in the *real* `opencode` runtime, and checks the things plugin authors actually care about: does it load, do its tools register, does it collide with other plugins, does it survive running next to a broken plugin, does it clean up, and what exactly gets installed. It does not touch your OpenCode installation, never mounts a development repository into a container, and runs entirely offline after the image is built. - **Default manifest works out of the box** — no external plugins required; it tests two tiny bundled example plugins. - **Bring your own plugin** — a local source directory, a packed tarball, or an already-built package, configurable by name and path. - **Test several together** — load-order permutations, tool-name collisions and failure isolation are generic. - **Optional regression profile** — reproduce the original three-plugin compatibility matrix without making those plugins a dependency of the lab. > The lab is a **standalone developer tool**, not a loadable OpenCode plugin. > See [Ecosystem & distribution](#ecosystem--distribution). --- ## Five-minute quick start ```sh git clone https://github.com/gitdamnit/opencode-plugin-lab cd opencode-plugin-lab make build # stage the bundled example plugins + build the Docker image make start # smoke-check the default configuration make suite # full generic suite across every configuration make report # print the latest report ``` `make discover` lists the plugins and configurations in the active manifest. ### Test your own plugin ```sh make test-plugin PLUGIN=/path/to/your-plugin ``` That generates a temporary single-plugin manifest, stages and builds your plugin, and runs the full generic suite. Nothing is committed. Add `NAME=...`, `TYPE=directory|package|tarball` or `ENTRY=index.js` to override the guesses. --- ## Requirements - Docker with Compose v2 (BuildKit) - A POSIX host with `bash`, `make`, `git`, `node` (the scripts are bash + Node ESM; macOS and Linux are supported, Windows via WSL2) - Network access **during `make build` only** (npm installs, base image, OpenCode CLI). Once built, every test runs with `network_mode: "none"`. ## Supported OpenCode versions | Version | Status | | --- | --- | | **2.0.21** | **Reproducible tested baseline.** The pinned version in every committed manifest and in the historical evidence. | | **2.0.32** | **Verified by evaluation** (`make build OPENCODE_VERSION=2.0.32 && make suite`): 76 pass / 0 fail / 5 skip, identical to 2.0.21. Not the pinned default. | The OpenCode V2 line moves quickly. The lab never silently follows `latest`: a manifest pins an exact version, `make build OPENCODE_VERSION=…` selects another for a one-off evaluation, and the **exact installed version is recorded in every report**. See [`docs/OPENCODE_COMPATIBILITY.md`](docs/OPENCODE_COMPATIBILITY.md). --- ## How it works (in one picture) ``` host container (opencode-plugin-lab:local, no network) lab.config.json ──► scripts/stage.mjs ──► /opt/lab/plugins/ (built lab packages) (manifest) staging// /opt/lab/harness/run.mjs (orchestrator) /opt/lab/lab.config.json (active manifest) reports/ ◄──────────── reports ◄───────── /lab/reports (bind mount, output only) /lab/{home,xdg,work} (tmpfs, disposable) ``` A manifest declares plugins and configurations. Staging copies each plugin's source (allowlisted, credential-scanned) into the build context; the builder installs dependencies and runs the plugin's build; the runtime image loads the built packages by absolute path through OpenCode's official `plugins` configuration. See [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). --- ## The default configurations `lab.config.json` ships four configurations and two example plugins: | Config | Plugins | What it proves | | --- | --- | --- | | `baseline` | none | the runtime boots cleanly with no external plugins | | `example-plugin` | `example-plugin` | a compiled plugin registers a tool and cleans up | | `single-plugin` | `example-plugin` (+ option override) | a single plugin with explicit options | | `multi-plugin` | `example-plugin`, `example-plugin-2` | a tool registerer **and** a no-tool plugin coexist | Test one: `make test CONFIG=multi-plugin TIER=validate`. ### Test tiers | Tier | What runs | | --- | --- | | `smoke` | server boots; plugins load; package inspection | | `functional` | smoke + package inspection | | `model` | offline model-request path via a local mock provider | | `integration` | smoke + load-order permutations | | `security` | configuration validation & error handling | | `validate` / `all` | everything: per-config runtime + model, plus every global suite | ### Global suites (run once, configuration-independent) | Suite | What it proves | | --- | --- | | `package-inspection` | package metadata, SDK resolution, entry point, build output, provenance | | `load-order` | every load-order permutation + duplicate entry; tool ids unique, no conflicts | | `failure-isolation` | a plugin that throws in `setup`, and one with an unresolvable import, loaded first and last — everything else stays healthy | | `process-cleanup` | graceful shutdown exits the process, releases the port, leaves no orphans | | `install-artifact` | the `npm pack`ed artifact (not just the build tree) loads in the runtime | | `config-validation` | bad configuration input is rejected with a useful error, not a crash | Capabilities are respected: a plugin that registers no tools is not failed for "missing tools" — the assertion is **skipped** and reported as such. --- ## Configuration schema and examples The full JSON Schema is [`schema/lab.config.schema.json`](schema/lab.config.schema.json); a walkthrough with copy-paste examples is [`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`](docs/CONFIGURATION.md). ```sh node scripts/lab-manifest.mjs validate # lint the default manifest node scripts/lab-manifest.mjs validate --manifest my-lab.config.json node scripts/lab-manifest.mjs discover # show sources/versions/commits ``` Minimal single-plugin manifest: ```jsonc { "$schema": "./schema/lab.config.schema.json", "version": 1, "plugins": [ { "name": "my-plugin", "source": { "type": "directory", "path": "../my-plugin" }, "build": { "command": "npm run build", "dist": "dist", "entry": "index.js" }, "capabilities": { "tools": true }, "expectTools": ["my_tool"] } ], "configs": [ { "name": "my-plugin", "plugins": ["my-plugin"] } ] } ``` Plugin inputs supported: `directory` (built), `package` (prebuilt, used as-is), `tarball` (a local `.tgz`), and `npm` (opt-in only via `allowRemote`; never fetched silently). No plugin is assumed to be in a particular npm scope, and public manifests contain no hardcoded home paths. --- ## Optional regression profile (three @gitdamnit plugins) The lab originally validated three independent plugins. That work is preserved as an **optional profile** — not a dependency of the default lab: ```sh make build PROFILE=gitdamnit # stage + build the three plugins make suite PROFILE=gitdamnit # full suite incl. their specialized assertions make test-checkpoint PROFILE=gitdamnit ``` Source paths default to `$HOME/Projects/...` and are overridable without editing the profile: ```sh CHECKPOINT_ORCHESTRATOR_DIR=... GIT_THAT_SHIT_DIR=... STRANGER_DANGER_DIR=... \ make build PROFILE=gitdamnit ``` See [`profiles/gitdamnit/README.md`](profiles/gitdamnit/README.md). The original `145 passed / 0 failed` run and its release-candidate evidence are **committed, unchanged, and clearly labelled as historical** under [`reports/historical/`](reports/historical/gitdamnit-2026-10-17/). They are not relabelled as validation of this generalized lab. --- ## Test extensions A manifest can add its own suites for a plugin-specific capability: - per-plugin: `"tests": ["tests/my-plugin.mjs"]` - manifest-wide: `"globalSuites": [{ "name": "my-suite", "module": "tests/suite.mjs" }]` Each module exports `run({ tier, plugin })`. See [`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#test-extensions) and the profile tests for complete examples. Extensions run **only** when their manifest is active — a fresh user never runs the three-plugin assertions. --- ## Reports Every run writes a dated, self-contained report and leaves the previous ones untouched: ``` reports/runs//test-report.json machine-readable (schema v1) reports/runs//test-report.md human-readable reports/test-report.{json,md} convenience pointer to the latest run ``` Reports record: the manifest (name, path, digest), OpenCode and Node versions, container image id, per-plugin version/commit/branch/dirty/source-type, the exact requested configuration, PASS/FAIL/SKIP counts by area, failures with logs, security warnings, and a reproduction command. Credentials are never written. `make rc-evidence` additionally produces `reports/rc-evidence.{json,md}`: source → staged → packed tarball (+ sha256) → installed-in-image, with a consistency check. --- ## Security model The offline `lab` service: `network_mode: "none"`, `read_only` rootfs with small tmpfs scratch mounts, all capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`, runs as your host uid/gid, no published ports, resource limits, `restart: "no"`. Only `./reports` is bind-mounted out; the plugin repositories are never mounted into a container. The only networked service is `lab-online`, behind the `online` profile, used exclusively by `make test-online`. Never mounted: host SSH/npm/cloud credentials, your real OpenCode configuration, entire home directories, or the Docker daemon socket. **Rootless Docker reduces risk but is not an absolute boundary against malicious plugin code.** Plugin source is built (dependencies + build scripts run) and then loaded by the runtime; review untrusted plugins before pointing the lab at them. Install-time lifecycle scripts are disabled by default (`install.scripts: false`); a plugin that needs them must opt in. See [`docs/SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md). --- ## Command reference ``` make help Show all commands make build Stage sources + build the image make stage Stage manifest sources only make discover Show plugin sources, versions, commits, configs make start Build if needed + smoke-check the default config make stop Stop lab containers make logs Container logs + latest report make test CONFIG=x TIER=y Run one configuration/tier make suite Full suite across every configuration make validate Full validation incl. all global suites make rc-evidence Source/packed/installed version evidence make test-plugin PLUGIN=… Build and test an arbitrary local plugin make profile PROFILE=… Build + full suite for an optional profile make test-online Optional online model test (.env required) make refresh Re-stage sources and rebuild make reset Reset disposable test data make report Print the latest report make shell Interactive shell in the lab container make clean Remove lab image, staged sources and reports ``` Select a manifest with `PROFILE=` (see `profiles/`) or `LAB_MANIFEST_FILE=`. --- ## Docker troubleshooting - **Rootless Docker** maps container UIDs into a subuid range, so a host-owned directory is not writable by a non-root container. `scripts/lib.sh` chmods `./reports` to `0777` for this reason; if a fresh run cannot write reports, check `docker info` reports `rootless`. - **`configured plugin path must be a directory`** — plugins are loaded as package directories, not file paths. - **`Cannot find package '@opencode/plugin'`** — a built package is missing its SDK dependency. Re-run `make build`; the builder installs it next to every plugin. - **Plugin shows `failed` in `/api/plugin`** — the report embeds the server log for failing suites; the plugin's `setup` most likely threw. - **A plugin build fails** — the image build fails loudly on purpose rather than shipping a stale artifact. Run `make discover` and check the staged source. --- ## Ecosystem & distribution This lab is a **standalone developer/testing tool**. It is not a loadable OpenCode runtime plugin, and it is not published to any plugin registry. It is distributed as source on GitHub and run with Docker. See [`docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`](docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md) for the publication procedure and the suggested repository description and topics. ## License MIT — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) and [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Change history: [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md).

# Disposable fixtures

The lab never runs destructive tests against a real project. Two kinds of
fixtures are used:

1. **Generated at runtime (primary).** The harness creates throwaway Git
   repositories and project directories under `/tmp` (a tmpfs inside the
   container) for every run. They are removed when the test finishes. This is
   what the Git That Shit restore/lock tests and the Checkpoint handoff test
   operate on.

2. **Templates in this directory (optional).** Static, non-secret templates that
   can be copied into a fixture project. `sample-project/` shows the minimal
   layout a disposable project needs. `synthetic-secrets.txt` contains clearly
   fake, well-known example values used by the Stranger Danger tests.

## Rules

- **Never** place real credentials here. The examples in
  `synthetic-secrets.txt` are public documentation placeholders.
- **Never** copy a live SQLite database as a "backup". The Checkpoint tests
  create fresh databases and the handoff test exports JSON, not a database file.
- Fixtures are excluded from the Docker build by allowlist; only this repo
  directory is copied to `/opt/lab/fixtures`.

# example-plugin-2

A second, even smaller example plugin. It registers **no tools** — only lifecycle
logging. It ships prebuilt (no build step), so it also exercises the lab's
`source.type: package` + `build.rootEntry` input path and the capability-aware
behaviour where tool assertions are *skipped* rather than failed.

Loaded together with `example-plugin` by the default `multi-plugin` configuration.

# example-plugin

A minimal, fully functional OpenCode V2 plugin that ships with the lab so a fresh
clone has something real to build, load and test.

- Registers exactly one tool: `example_echo`
- Logs on `setup` and on unload (lifecycle)
- Makes no network calls, needs no API keys, writes nothing to disk
- Built with `tsc`; the lab packages `dist/` for OpenCode to load

It exists only to exercise the generic lab. Put your own plugin alongside it and
point a manifest at it — see the top-level `README.md` and `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`.

# Regression profile: three @gitdamnit plugins

This optional profile reproduces the lab's original purpose: validating three
independently developed OpenCode V2 plugins together.

It is **not** required to use the lab, and the plugins are **not** downloaded by
default. It exists so the historical regression work stays reproducible without
making any of the three plugins a dependency of the lab.

## Activate

```sh
make build PROFILE=gitdamnit
make suite PROFILE=gitdamnit
```

Individual configurations:

```sh
make test-checkpoint PROFILE=gitdamnit
make test-git-that-shit PROFILE=gitdamnit
make test-stranger-danger PROFILE=gitdamnit
make test-all PROFILE=gitdamnit
```

## Source locations

`lab.config.json` here points at the maintainer's worktrees by default. Override
without editing anything:

```sh
CHECKPOINT_ORCHESTRATOR_DIR=/path/to/checkpoint-orchestrator \
GIT_THAT_SHIT_DIR=/path/to/git-that-shit \
STRANGER_DANGER_DIR=/path/to/stranger-danger \
  make build PROFILE=gitdamnit
```

The exact commits built are recorded in every report. To build from a specific
historical commit without modifying the source repo, export it read-only first:

```sh
git -C /path/to/checkpoint-orchestrator archive 65bf698 | (mkdir -p /tmp/pin/cp && tar -x -C /tmp/pin/cp)
CHECKPOINT_ORCHESTRATOR_DIR=/tmp/pin/cp make build PROFILE=gitdamnit
```

## What is preserved here

- `tests/` — the plugin-specific suites, moved here from `harness/tests/`
  unchanged except for import paths: functional suites for each plugin, plus the
  shared `security`, `concurrency`, `combined` and `checkpoint-triggers` suites.
- `tests/workers/` — the multi-process workers used by the concurrency suite.
- `configs/legacy/` — the original per-plugin `opencode.jsonc` files, kept for
  reference. They are superseded by the generated configurations but are not
  deleted.
- `plugins.tsv` — the original source map, kept as historical reference.

# Changelog

All notable changes to OpenCode Plugin Lab are recorded here. This project uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-16

First generalized, standalone release. The lab no longer depends on any specific
plugin.

### Added

- **Manifest-driven architecture.** A single `lab.config.json` declares plugins
  (source directory / prebuilt package / tarball / opt-in npm), their
  capabilities and expected tools, the configurations to run, and optional test
  extensions. Full JSON Schema in `schema/lab.config.schema.json`.
- **Manifest CLI** (`scripts/lab-manifest.mjs`): `validate`, `plan`, `discover`,
  `configs`, `versions` — one shared implementation used by every script.
- **Bundled example plugins** (`examples/example-plugin`, `examples/example-plugin-2`):
  a compiled TypeScript plugin that registers a safe tool with lifecycle logging,
  and a prebuilt JavaScript plugin that registers no tools (exercising
  capability-aware skipping).
- **Generic test suites**:
  `package-inspection`, `load-order` (all permutations + duplicate entry +
  tool-conflict detection), `failure-isolation`, `process-cleanup`,
  `install-artifact` (pack + load the artifact), `config-validation`, and a
  capability-aware `runtime-load` and `model-path`.
- **Default configurations**: `baseline`, `example-plugin`, `single-plugin`,
  `multi-plugin`.
- **`make test-plugin PLUGIN=<path>`** to build and test an arbitrary local
  plugin with no committed manifest.
- **Optional regression profile** `profiles/gitdamnit/` for the three original
  `@gitdamnit` plugins, with their specialized tests relocated (not deleted).
- **Dated run archives**: every run writes `reports/runs/<run-id>/` and never
  overwrites earlier evidence.
- **Documentation**: `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`,
  `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, refreshed `README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
  `docs/SECURITY.md`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **ProDoc Guard** project memory: `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md`, `DECISION_LOG.md`,
  `PROJECT_STATUS.md`.

### Verified

- OpenCode V2 **2.0.21** (pinned baseline) and **2.0.32** (evaluated): the full
  generic suite passes identically on both — 76 pass / 0 fail / 5 skip. See
  `reports/v1.0.0/` and `docs/OPENCODE_COMPATIBILITY.md`.

### Changed

- The Docker builder is now driven by a resolved build plan
  (`staging/_build/plan.json`) instead of a hardcoded list of three plugins.
- Dependency installation disables npm lifecycle scripts by default
  (`--ignore-scripts`), opt-in per plugin.
- Reports carry manifest name/path/digest, image id, per-plugin source type, and
  security warnings.
- Commands were preserved: `help build stage discover start stop logs test suite
  validate rc-evidence test-online refresh reset report shell clean`.

### Preserved (not changed by this release)

- The original three-plugin regression evidence
  (`reports/historical/gitdamnit-2026-10-17/`) is committed unchanged and clearly
  labelled as historical: **145 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, OpenCode

- The three `@gitdamnit` plugins remain independent products. The lab is not a

# Decision Log

## How to Use This Log

1. Copy the block below to the end of the `## Decisions` section.
2. Use the next free four-digit ID. IDs are never reused and never renumbered.
3. Date the record the day the decision was actually made (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
4. Record the alternatives you rejected and why. A decision without context is a
   rumour, not a record.
5. Never rewrite history. If a decision changes, append a superseding record.

```markdown
### D-0001 — Short imperative title

- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** the situation and the constraint that forced a choice
- **Alternatives Considered:** option A (rejected because ...), option B (rejected because ...)
- **Decision:** what was decided, in one or two sentences
- **Rationale:** why this option wins, including what it costs
- **Consequences:** what follows from it — new constraints, follow-up work, risks
- **Supersedes:** None
```

Allowed statuses: `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Superseded`, `Deprecated`, `Rejected`.

## Decisions

### D-0001 — Drive the lab from a declarative JSONC manifest

- **Date:** 2026-10-16
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** The lab hardcoded three plugins, their tools, ids, configs and
  specialized tests. A fresh user could not use it without those plugins.
- **Alternatives Considered:** Environment variables only (rejected: no structure,
  no validation, awkward for multiple plugins); a TypeScript config module
  (rejected: executes code before anything is validated, and adds a build step to
  the host); keeping hardcoded defaults plus env overrides (rejected: still
  assumes the three plugins).
- **Decision:** One `lab.config.json` (JSONC) per manifest declares plugins,
  sources, capabilities, expected tools, configurations and extensions, validated
  against `schema/lab.config.schema.json`.
- **Rationale:** Data is inspectable, diffable, lintable and portable. A single
  loader (`harness/lib/manifest.mjs`) is shared by every script, so staging,
  discovery, build and the harness cannot diverge. Cost: one more concept to
  learn, mitigated by a validator with actionable errors and examples.
- **Consequences:** All downstream tooling is manifest-driven; the old
  `plugins.tsv` and per-config JSONC files become reference artefacts.
- **Supersedes:** None

### D-0002 — Generate OpenCode configs at run time

- **Date:** 2026-10-16
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** Configs were baked JSONC templates with hardcoded plugin paths.
- **Alternatives Considered:** Templating the old JSONC files with placeholders
  (rejected: still per-plugin files, still requires editing); baking generated
  configs at build time (rejected: cannot support a manifest supplied at run
  time, e.g. `make test-plugin`).
- **Decision:** `harness/lib/opencode.mjs#generateConfig` builds each
  `opencode.json` from the manifest, appending the lab inspector last. An
  optional JSONC `template` supplies non-plugin settings.
- **Rationale:** The plugin list lives in exactly one place (the manifest);
  non-plugin settings remain expressible. The old per-plugin JSONC files are kept

# Product Requirements

## Project Identity

**Name:** OpenCode Plugin Lab
**Repository:** https://github.com/gitdamnit/opencode-plugin-lab
**Licence:** MIT
**Maintainer:** gitdamnit

## Purpose

OpenCode V2 plugin authors have no easy way to prove that a plugin loads in the
real runtime and behaves safely alongside other plugins. Manual testing inside a
personal OpenCode installation is unreproducible, leaks credentials, and cannot
show failure isolation, load-order collisions, or install provenance.

OpenCode Plugin Lab exists to make that verification reproducible, disposable,
and safe: point it at any plugin, and it builds and loads the plugin in the real
`opencode` runtime inside an isolated, offline container, then reports exactly
what happened and what was installed.

## Intended Users

- **OpenCode plugin authors** who want a repeatable pass/fail before publishing.
- **Maintainers reviewing third-party plugins** who need a sandboxed smoke test.
- **CI pipelines** that need to gate a plugin on real-runtime behaviour.

They already know Node, npm and Docker, and are comfortable editing a JSON
manifest. They expect commands to be simple (`make …`) and results to be honest.

# Architecture

## Overview

```
host                                          container (opencode-plugin-lab:local, no network)
lab.config.json  ──► scripts/stage.mjs ─────►  /opt/lab/plugins/<name>      (built lab packages)
  (active manifest)   staging/<name>/          /opt/lab/lab.config.json     (active manifest)
                      staging/_build/plan.json /opt/lab/harness/run.mjs     (orchestrator)
                                               /opt/lab/{profiles,schema,examples}
reports/runs/<id>/ ◄──────── reports ◄──────── /lab/reports (bind mount, output only)
                                               /lab/{home,xdg,work} (tmpfs, disposable)
```

Nothing is hardcoded per plugin. The manifest names plugins, sources,
capabilities, expected tools and configurations; everything downstream is
derived.

## Manifest → plan → build

1. `scripts/stage.mjs --manifest <manifest>` loads and validates the manifest,
   resolves each plugin's source (expanding `~`, `$HOME`, `${VAR:-default}`),
   copies an allowlisted view of it into `staging/<name>/`, scans for
   credential-like files, records provenance into `LAB_SOURCE.json`, and writes
   `staging/_build/plan.json`.
2. `docker/build-plugins.mjs` reads the plan and, per plugin, installs
   dependencies (npm lifecycle scripts disabled unless opted in), runs the build,
   and assembles `/out/plugins/<name>/`:

   ```
   compiled :  index.ts (shim)  dist/…  package.json  node_modules/  upstream-package.json  LAB_SOURCE.json
   prebuilt :  <package files>  package.json  node_modules/  upstream-package.json  LAB_SOURCE.json
   ```

   `index.ts` exists because OpenCode's local-directory loader uses a directory
   entry, not `package.json#main`. The lab inspector is built the same way.
3. The runtime image bakes the built packages, the harness, and **all**
   manifests (`lab.config.json`, `profiles/`, `schema/`, `examples/`).

## Manifest → runtime config

`harness/lib/opencode.mjs#generateConfig` builds each `opencode.json` from the
manifest: the plugin list (absolute package dirs + options), an optional JSONC
template for non-plugin settings, and the lab inspector appended last.

## Loading model

OpenCode V2 loads plugins from the `plugins` array in `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{ "package": "/opt/lab/plugins/my-plugin", "options": { … } }
```

`opencode` resolves `@opencode/plugin` relative to the plugin directory, which is
why each built package carries its own `node_modules`.

## Isolation model

- **Per configuration:** its own project directory and HOME/XDG trees under
  `/lab/work/runs/<config>/…`, so session databases, plugin state and logs never
  mix. The run directory is deleted at the start of each boot.
- **Per run:** reports are archived under `reports/runs/<run-id>/`; the previous
  run is never overwritten.
- **Per container:** `/lab` and `/tmp` are tmpfs; `make reset` discards
  everything.

## Verification strategy

| Layer | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime loading | `opencode serve` + `GET /api/plugin`; plugins matched by source path (or id) |
| Tool registration | `lab.inspector` reads `ctx.tool.list()` during `setup` |
| Load order & conflicts | all permutations of the widest config + a duplicate entry |
| Failure isolation | broken plugins (throw / unresolvable import) first and last |
| Process cleanup | shutdown exits, port released, no orphan processes |
| Package & provenance | entry resolution, SDK presence, build output, commit/version |
| Install from artifact | `npm pack` the built package, extract, load in the runtime |
| Configuration validation | bad input rejected with an actionable error |
| Model-request path | local OpenAI-compatible mock captures the outbound body |
| Write boundaries | disposable project's top-level entries checked against expectations |

Global suites run **once** per invocation. Per-plugin (`tests`) and manifest-wide
(`globalSuites`) extensions run only while their manifest is active.

## Failure handling

- A plugin that fails to build fails the image build (no silent fallback).
- A plugin that fails to load is reported by `/api/plugin` as `failed`, and the
  runtime suite fails with the server log attached.
- Test failures do not stop the orchestrator; every configuration runs and the
  process exits non-zero if any test failed.
- Capabilities that a plugin does not declare are **skipped**, never faked.

# Configuration

Everything the lab does is driven by a single **manifest** — a JSONC file that
declares which plugins to test and how to run them. The default is
[`lab.config.json`](../lab.config.json); optional profiles live under
`profiles/`. The machine-readable schema is
[`schema/lab.config.schema.json`](../schema/lab.config.schema.json).

Validate any manifest with:

```sh
node scripts/lab-manifest.mjs validate --manifest path/to/lab.config.json
```

`validate` prints actionable errors (unknown plugin referenced by a config,
missing `source.type`, a path that references an unset variable, a `tests` module
that does not exist, contradictions between `expectTools` and
`capabilities.tools`, …).

---

## Top-level shape

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./schema/lab.config.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "name": "my lab",
  "opencode": { "version": "2.0.21", "sdkVersion": "2.0.21" },
  "defaultConfig": "baseline",
  "plugins": [ /* see below */ ],
  "configs": [ /* see below */ ],
  "globalSuites": [ /* optional, see Test extensions */ ]
}
```

- `version` must be `1`.
- `opencode.version` pins `@opencode/cli`; `sdkVersion` pins `@opencode/plugin`
  and defaults to `version`. `make build OPENCODE_VERSION=…` overrides for a
  one-off evaluation; the exact installed version is recorded in every report.
- `defaultConfig` is what `make start` and a bare `make test` run.

## A plugin

```jsonc
{
  "name": "my-plugin",                     // required, stable lab id
  "package": "@me/my-plugin",              // optional, informational
  "id": "me.my-plugin",                    // optional runtime plugin id
  "source": { "type": "directory", "path": "../my-plugin" },
  "build": { "command": "npm run build", "dist": "dist", "entry": "index.js" },
  "options": { "greeting": "hi" },         // passed to the plugin at load
  "capabilities": { "tools": true },
  "expectTools": ["my_tool"],
  "setupMarker": "[my-plugin] setup",      // optional: asserted in the log
  "cleanupMarker": "[my-plugin] cleanup",  // optional: asserted after shutdown
  "expectedWrites": [".my-plugin-state"],  // optional: allowed project writes
  "tests": ["tests/my-plugin.mjs"],        // optional: plugin-specific suite
  "notes": "free text recorded in reports"
}
```

### Source types

| `type` | Meaning | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | a local source tree | dependencies installed and the build command run |
| `package` | an already-built package directory | used as-is (set `build.rootEntry: true`) |
| `tarball` | a local `.tgz` | extracted; built unless `rootEntry` |
| `npm` | an npm reference (`name@1.2.3`) | **never fetched** unless `source.allowRemote: true` |

Paths are resolved relative to the manifest file and support `~`, `$HOME`,
`${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}`. Public manifests should not contain absolute
home paths — use a variable with a default:

```jsonc
"source": { "type": "directory", "path": "${MY_PLUGIN_DIR:-$HOME/Projects/my-plugin}" }
```

If a source is not a git worktree (an exported tree, a tarball), record the commit
it corresponds to so provenance is complete:

```jsonc
"source": { "type": "directory", "path": "/tmp/pin/my-plugin", "commit": "65bf6981eee5…" }
```

### Build shapes

- **Compiled** (default): `build.command` runs (or the package's own `build`
  script), and `dist/<entry>` is packaged behind an `index.ts` shim.
- **Prebuilt**: set `build.rootEntry: true` and point `entry` at the file at the
  package root (e.g. `index.js`). No build runs.

`install.scripts` (default `false`) controls whether npm lifecycle scripts run
during dependency installation. Enable it only for plugins that need it; it is a
supply-chain risk.

### Capabilities

The harness only asserts what a plugin declares, and reports the rest as skipped:

```jsonc
"capabilities": { "tools": false, "hooks": false, "storage": false, "redaction": false, "network": false }
```

- `tools` — registers tools; `expectTools` lists their ids.
- `redaction` — transforms model requests; the offline model-path suite then
  asserts a synthetic secret is absent from the transmitted request.
- `network` — makes outbound calls; only exercised in the gated online tier.
- `storage` — keeps its own state; the generic write-boundary check covers it.

## A configuration

```jsonc
{
  "name": "multi-plugin",
  "description": "two plugins together",
  "plugins": ["my-plugin", "another-plugin"],       // load order
  "options": { "my-plugin": { "greeting": "hi" } },  // per-plugin overrides
  "settings": { "compaction": { "auto": false } },   // extra opencode keys
  "template": "configs/base.opencode.jsonc"          // optional JSONC base
}
```

The plugin list is always generated from the manifest. `settings` and `template`
let you add non-plugin runtime keys (providers, compaction, …). A `template` may
use the `__REPORTS__` placeholder; the generated plugin list and the lab
inspector are applied on top of it.

## Test extensions

Per-plugin suite (`"tests"`) — runs once, gated on the plugin being built:

```js
// tests/my-plugin.mjs
import { Suite, assert } from "../../../harness/lib/suite.mjs";
import { PLUGINS } from "../../../harness/lib/env.mjs";
import { join } from "node:path";

export async function run({ tier = "validate", plugin }) {
  const suite = new Suite(`plugin/${plugin}`, { tier });
  await suite.test("my-plugin.smoke", () => {
    assert(PLUGINS[plugin].tools.length > 0, "declares tools");
    return { packageDir: PLUGINS[plugin].packageDir };
  });
  return suite.summary();
}
```

Manifest-wide suite (`"globalSuites"`):

```jsonc
"globalSuites": [{ "name": "my-suite", "module": "tests/my-suite.mjs" }]
```

Both shapes export `run({ tier, plugin, name })` and return a `Suite#summary()`.
Extensions run **only when their manifest is active**, so a fresh clone never
runs them.

   tested, never to the plugins this lab merely observes.

# Security notes

The lab is designed to test security- and state-sensitive plugins without
exposing the host or any real data. It does **not** claim to be a hard sandbox.

## Container hardening (`lab` service)

| Control | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Networking | `network_mode: "none"` — no DNS, no outbound, loopback only |
| Privileges | `cap_drop: ["ALL"]`, `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]` |
| Filesystem | `read_only: true` rootfs; scratch via tmpfs (`/lab/{home,xdg,work}`, `/tmp`, `/run`) |
| User | runs as the invoking host uid/gid (non-root) |
| Privileged mode | never used |
| Docker socket | never mounted |
| Host networking | never used |
| Ports | none published; the server binds `127.0.0.1` inside the container |
| Restart | `restart: "no"` |
| Limits | `mem_limit`, `cpus`, `pids_limit` |

## Host surface

- **No mount of any development repository into a container.** Plugin sources are
  copied into `staging/` at build time; only built artifacts reach the image.
- **Only `./reports` is bind-mounted** into the container, and only for output.
- A selected manifest file may be mounted read-only over its baked path so edits
  are never stale.
- All test state (databases, shadow repos, audit logs, fixtures) lives on tmpfs
  and is discarded with the container.

## What is never staged or shipped

`scripts/stage.mjs` excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, `.github`, build output,
coverage, images, logs, `.opencode`, and **every `.env*`**, then aborts if a
credential-like file (`.env*`, `auth.json`, `credentials*`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa*`)
is found in the staged tree. `.dockerignore` additionally excludes `.env*`, key
material, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.config/opencode`, `.opencode` and `.lab`.

## Credentials

- The lab never reads credentials from an existing OpenCode installation
  (`~/.config/opencode`, `auth.json`, `~/.local/share/opencode`).
- The optional online tier reads a **dedicated test credential** only from
  `.env` (see `.env.example`). The value is passed as an environment variable to
  the single `lab-online` container and is never logged or written to reports.
- All functional tests use clearly synthetic, non-functional placeholders.

## Supply chain

- Dependency installation runs with `--ignore-scripts` by default. A plugin that
  needs lifecycle scripts must set `install.scripts: true` in the manifest — an
  explicit, documented supply-chain decision.
- A `source.type: npm` plugin is **never** fetched unless `source.allowRemote`
  is `true`; the default refuses.
- Building a plugin source inevitably runs *its build*, which may execute
  arbitrary code. Review untrusted plugins before pointing the lab at them.

## Shell argument handling

Host scripts quote all arguments and pass manifest-derived values through arrays
(`mapfile`), not unquoted interpolation. The container runs the harness with
fixed arguments. No manifest field is passed to `eval` except the manifest's
`opencode` version, which is read into `OPENCODE_VERSION`/`PLUGIN_SDK_VERSION`
and constrained by the manifest schema's version pattern.

## Scope of `reset` / `clean`

- `make reset` removes only this compose project's containers and generated
  reports (keeping `reports/historical/`).
- `make clean` additionally removes the lab image, `staging/` and generated
  reports. It never touches other Docker resources, any repository, or the
  committed historical evidence.

## Known limitations (also listed in every report)

- **Rootless Docker reduces risk but is not an absolute boundary against
  malicious plugin code.** A container escape or a resource-exhaustion attack is
  still possible in principle.
- Outbound redaction is verified on the supported HTTP model-request path using a
  local mock provider. Provider-native WebSocket traffic is not covered.
- Hook registration is observed indirectly (tool registration + the model path);
  OpenCode exposes no API to enumerate hooks.
- A plugin’s own persistence is exercised only through the generic
  write-boundary check, not a plugin-specific storage audit.
